Sebi forms panel to review listing norms khushboo tiwari Mumbai, 16 November The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) has con- stituted a sub-group of its Pri- mary Market Advisory Committee (PMAC) to review provisions governing initial public offerings (IPOs), follow- on public offers (FPOs), pref- erential issues and qualiﬁed institutional placements (QIPs), with a focus on sim- plifying regulations and easing access to capital mar- kets for eligible issuers. The sub-group will review Sebi’s Issue of Capital and Dis- closure Requirements Regu- lations, 2018. The regulator plans to rationalise regulatory requirements, eliminate duplicative disclosures and procedures, and improve regulatory clarity and consistency. The review will cover eligi- bility conditions for issuers across different modes of capital raising, lock-in requirements applicable to promoters and pre-issue capital, and application, allocation and allotment mechanisms. The panel will also exam- ine disclosure requirements in offer documents and other prescribed ﬁlings, pricing norms and price discovery frameworks, including deter- mination and disclosure of price bands and ﬂoor prices. The panel is chaired by NSE managing director and chief executive officer Ashish Chauhan. Its members include representatives from BSE, the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India, the Institute of Company Secre- taries of India, ICICI Securities, Kotak Investment Banking, Khaitan & Co, S&R Associates, Stakeholder Empowerment Services and CII. The sub-group may co-opt additional members or invite subject matter experts and stakeholders. Its recommen- dations will be placed before PMAC for consideration.vvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvv
